needs.title: Needs → wants → demands
needs.description: A need takes a specific form as a want; purchasing power makes it demand.

stp.title: Choose whom to serve and what to promise
stp.description: Segmentation, targeting and positioning, with two tasks in each stage.

supply.title: Manage flows and relationships together
supply.description: Physical goods generally move downstream and requirements upstream. Information also travels both ways.

integration.title: The scope of integration expands
integration.description: Baseline, functional, internal and external integration.

fourrs.title: Four Rs, four distinct questions
fourrs.description: Responsiveness, reliability, resilience and relationships each address a different requirement.

costvalue.title: Two sources of competitive advantage
costvalue.description: A cost and value advantage can be combined. Both dimensions increase toward the preferred high-high position.

experience.title: Experience concerns cumulative output
experience.description: Illustrative unit cost declines as cumulative output increases. This is not a measured dataset.

valuechain.title: Porter’s value chain
valuechain.description: Four support activities span five primary activities. Each contributes to value and cost.

vrin.title: Four tests for a sustained resource advantage
vrin.description: Valuable, rare, imperfectly imitable and non-substitutable. All tests require analysis in context.

ara.title: ARA: who, what and doing
ara.description: Actor bonds, resource ties and activity links influence one another.

interaction.title: IMP: interaction sits inside a wider context
interaction.description: Organisations and individuals exchange products, information, finance and social contact within an atmosphere and environment.

networklevels.title: Three layers across three analysis levels
networklevels.description: ARA layers and relationship, small-world, wider-world levels are different dimensions.

makebuy.title: Ownership and coordination are different choices
makebuy.description: Market contracting, quasi-integration and vertical integration form a continuum.

tiers.title: A supplier base has structure, not just a count
tiers.description: Tier-one suppliers interface with the focal firm and coordinate lower-tier suppliers.

kraljic.title: Kraljic’s purchasing portfolio
kraljic.description: Profit impact rises upward; supply risk rises rightward.

kraljicprocess.title: The matrix starts a wider management process
kraljicprocess.description: Classification is followed by market analysis, strategic positioning and action plans.

transformation.title: Operations transform inputs into outcomes
transformation.description: Inputs pass through transformation to outputs. Feedback improves future decisions.

timeprocess.title: Follow elapsed time, not only processing time
timeprocess.description: Teaching example: four hours of activity plus twelve hours waiting, then six waiting hours removed.

fishbone.title: Organise possible causes before testing them
fishbone.description: People, machines, material and methods are investigation categories, not proof of causation.

ptime.title: Can the full process fit the customer’s wait?
ptime.description: Illustrative source-make-deliver time totals eight days while acceptable wait is three.

postpone.title: Delay differentiation, preserve options
postpone.description: A common base becomes order-specific only when useful information is known.

leagile.title: Lean upstream · agile downstream
leagile.description: The customer order decoupling point separates common forecast-supported work from order-specific response.

generic.title: Match strategy to demand and supply timing
generic.description: Demand predictability is horizontal; long supply lead time is above short supply lead time.

costtypes.title: Three independent cost dimensions
costtypes.description: Fixed/variable, direct/indirect, engineered/discretionary classify different properties.

breakeven.title: Break-even: contribution covers fixed cost
breakeven.description: Illustrative linear chart: F=1200, p=15, v=9; break-even is 200 shirts.

reorder.title: Reorder before the stock is exhausted
reorder.description: Q=600, demand=40/day, lead=5 days, safety=60, ROP=260. Schematic sawtooth.

eoq.title: EOQ balances opposing costs
eoq.description: Ordering falls as Q increases; holding rises; their sum has an optimum at Q=600 in the worked example.

abc.title: Prioritise attention by annual usage value
abc.description: Illustrative five-item dataset totals €10,000; the first item contributes €8,000.

systems.title: Information tools support different decisions
systems.description: ERP integrates processes; MPS plans output; MRP plans material; WMS supports warehouse execution.

negotiationpie.title: Divide value · create value
negotiationpie.description: Distributive bargaining and integrative problem solving can occur in the same negotiation.

phases.title: Agreement is not finished until it is implemented
phases.description: Preparation, greeting, introduction, argumentation, compromise, closure and realisation.
